description: Shared golden vectors for the %gw-btc kelvin-9 (OP_RETURN) formats. The authority is the Hoon desk; values were computed with `urbit eval` against zuse's secp tagged hash and jam, and cross-checked in Python. Consumed by the Hoon tests (groundwire/tests/lib/gw-btc-pass.hoon), Causeway web (TS), and Causeway desktop (Python). All three MUST agree with this file byte-for-byte.

conventions.tagged_hash: H_tag(tag, msg) = sha256(sha256(tag) || sha256(tag) || msg); tag is the ASCII tag string; output is 32 big-endian bytes.
conventions.jam: A jammed noun is serialized to its minimal little-endian byte string. In this file every `jam_*_le` field is that byte string in hex (first byte = least significant. Tagged-hash preimages consume a jam in exactly this little-endian byte order (matching the Hoon lib's jam-octs); do NOT byte-reverse). A noun is an atom (unsigned int) or a cell [head, tail]; cells right-associate: [a b c] == [a [b c]].
conventions.unit: (unit x): the null unit ~ is the atom 0; a full unit [~ v] is the cell [0, v].
conventions.dat: dat = can(0, [mat(dom), mat(9), [256, d]]) — bit-level: mat-encoded domain tag at bit 0, then mat-encoded kelvin 9, then exactly 256 bits of d. `dat` below is the resulting atom in big-endian hex. Decoders reject trailing data.
conventions.blind: blind = H_tag('gw/spawn-blind', seed_le_bytes)  (seed as its minimal little-endian byte string)
conventions.state_leaf: tapleaf, version 0xc0, script = OP_RETURN PUSH2 'gw' PUSH32 c = bytes 6a 02 67 77 20 || c (37 bytes). Single-leaf tree: merkle root == TapLeaf hash.
conventions.state_output_key_q: Q = taproot output key = x-coordinate of lift_x(P) + H_tag('TapTweak', x(P) || leafhash)*G, where P is the 33-byte compressed internal key and leafhash is the TapLeaf hash of the state leaf. The sat-carrying output's scriptPubKey is OP_1 PUSH32 Q.
conventions.publication: OP_RETURN output script = OP_RETURN PUSH3 'urb' PUSH1 kelvin(0x09) <pushdata payload>; payload = jam([pass, opening]) as little-endian bytes.  The pass carries the comet's FULL custody log in its xtr (see with_xtr); the opening describes the hop the carrying transaction performs.  MAX_PUBLICATION = 1024 bytes in all three implementations.
conventions.pushdata: The payload push is minimal: length <= 75 -> a direct push (the opcode IS the length); length <= 255 -> OP_PUSHDATA1, bytes 4c || len; otherwise -> OP_PUSHDATA2, bytes 4d || len as TWO bytes LITTLE-ENDIAN (lo, hi). A fief-carrying publication is 265-269 bytes, so OP_PUSHDATA2 is the ordinary case, not an edge case. Anything an OP_PUSHDATA2 cannot express, or a payload over the 512-byte cap, is a hard error in every implementation -- never a truncated length byte.
conventions.opening: opening = [internal_key, snapshot, blind_opening]; blind_opening = (unit [spawn_sont, blind]) — present marks a spawn, absent (0) a state update.
conventions.blind_opening: [spawn_sont, start_height, blind] — start_height is the block height of the spawn transaction (transport metadata; NOT in any hash preimage).
conventions.snapshot: snapshot = [life, rift, key, sponsor, fief]; sponsor = (unit @p); fief = (unit fief); key is the messaging key (cry.pub of the suite-C pass). As a noun: [life [rift [key [sponsor fief]]]].
conventions.custody_entry: custody log entry = [txid, height, opening] where opening = (unit opening). xtr = jam(list of entries, oldest first).
conventions.fief: (unit fief); fief = [%turf p q] | [%if p q] | [%is p q]. As a noun: [tag, [p, q]], tag being the term's own little-endian cord atom (%if = 26217, %is = 29545, %turf = 1718903156). For %if, p is the IPv4 address as its ordinary big-endian 32-bit integer (.64.227.13.22 = 1088621846) and q is the UDP port. Absent in the `basic` and `state-key-pin` vectors; present in `pushdata2-fief`.
conventions.with_xtr: with_xtr(pass, xtr): re-encode a suite-%c pass around a different xtr tail.  Layout is 'c'(8 bits) | ugn(256) | cry(256) | mat(dat) | xtr, with xtr riding at its exact bit length ((met 0 xtr)) and OMITTED entirely when 0.  ugn, cry and dat are copied verbatim, so fig (the @p) is unchanged: xtr is outside the key tweak.  Mirrors +with-xtr:gw-btc-pass, pass_with_xtr() in causeway.py and passWithXtr() in src/spawn/mine-c.ts.

publication.note: publication = [pass, [internal_key, snapshot, blind_opening]]; here pass=0xdeadbeefcafe, internal_key=0x2cafe, snapshot as above, blind_opening=[spawn_sont, start_height=778000, blind]

xtr.note: two entries oldest-first: entry0 = [txid=0x123...def0, height=778000, opening (full, with blind_opening)], entry1 = [txid=0xfeedface, height=778010, opening=~]

vectors.name: state-key-pin
vectors.note: For the +state-key Hoon golden test: the sponsor=null snapshot [life=1 rift=0 key=0xabcd sponsor=~ fief=~], its commitment, leaf, and the taproot output key Q for internal key P=02||secp.G.x.

vectors.name: pushdata2-fief
vectors.note: THE OP_PUSHDATA2 VECTOR. A realistic public spawn: a real 108-byte suite-%c pass (minted over the `dat` below with an empty xtr), a snapshot committing a fief, and a full blind-opening. That jams to 269 bytes -- past the 255-byte ceiling of OP_PUSHDATA1 -- so op_return_script uses OP_PUSHDATA2: bytes `4d 0d 01`, a TWO-byte LITTLE-ENDIAN 269. Every fief-carrying publication measured in the field is 265-269 bytes, so this is the ordinary shape, not an edge case; before kelvin-9's encoders learned 0x4d, Hoon silently truncated the length byte here and Causeway raised. `key` in the snapshot is the pass's own cry.pub, as a real publication carries. Cross-checked: Hoon (`urbit eval` over lib/gw-btc-pass.hoon) and Python (causeway/desktop/causeway.py) produce byte-identical jam_publication_le and op_return_script.

publication.note: publication = [pass, [internal_key, snapshot, blind_opening]]; blind_opening = [spawn_sont, start_height=961059, blind]. pass_bytes/payload_bytes are byte lengths of the hex fields below, given so a reader can see 269 > 255 without counting.

vectors.name: full-packet
vectors.note: THE FULL-PACKET VECTOR, and the reason MAX_PUBLICATION had to rise. A kelvin-9 publication is the comet's whole attestation packet: `pass` is byte-for-byte the pass it hands a peer over ames -- the same 108-byte suite-%c pass as pushdata2-fief, re-encoded with the custody log below in its `xtr` -- and `opening` is the hop the carrying transaction performs, which the payload cannot name because its txid does not exist until the transaction is signed. A watcher completes the log with [txid height opening] from the block it is reading, giving seven hops. Six carried hops jam to 392 bytes of xtr, a 500-byte pass and a 588-byte payload: over the old 512-byte cap and well inside the new 1024. Hoon (+with-xtr / +make-publication:gw-btc-pass), Causeway desktop (Python) and Causeway web (TS) must all produce these exact bytes.
